what: UDR owns about 60,000 apartments across the United States, split between coastal cities and Sun Belt markets, and rents them on one-year leases.
customers: Renters in Washington, Boston, New York, California, Florida and Texas.
money: new developments and joint venture income
moat: A portfolio balanced between coastal markets, where building is almost impossible, and Sun Belt markets, where demand grows: the mix smooths what either alone would not.
risks: $6.0B of debt against almost no cash
Sun Belt supply has slowed rent growth in roughly half the portfolio
Revenue has been flat at $1.7B for two years
opportunities: $614M of free cash flow and a 22.1% net margin
Coastal markets have almost no new supply and rents there have kept rising
Analysts see about 13% upside, with 21 covering the stock
watch: Same-store revenue growth split between coastal and Sun Belt markets.
